```{r setup}
library(lactater)
```

lactater turns the stages of a step test into lactate thresholds, checks them, and puts them to use: training zones,
training load, and comparisons between tests.
`r if (identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")) "Click the steps below to unfold them."`

```{r workflow, echo = FALSE, eval = identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true") && requireNamespace("collapsibleTree", quietly = TRUE)}
steps <- read.csv(text = '
step,tool,detail
"1. Collect","One row per stage","intensity, lactate, HR, RPE"
"1. Collect","One row per stage","resting sample at intensity 0"
"1. Collect","lactate_tests","15 tests, 4 sports"
"2. Estimate","lactate_threshold()","Log-log"
"2. Estimate","lactate_threshold()","OBLA (fixed lactate)"
"2. Estimate","lactate_threshold()","Bsln+ (rise above baseline)"
"2. Estimate","lactate_threshold()","Dmax family"
"2. Estimate","lactate_threshold()","LTP1 and LTP2"
"2. Estimate","lactate_threshold()","LTratio and IAT"
"2. Estimate","ci = TRUE","bootstrap confidence intervals"
"3. Check","lactate_checks()","dips, plateaus, missing rest"
"3. Check","lactate_diagnostics()","residuals, influence, jackknife"
"3. Check","lactate_fit_quality()","which curve predicts best"
"4. Look","autoplot()","all methods, or one"
"4. Look","lactate_report()","a table for reports"
"5. Use","lactate_zones()","3 or 5 zones"
"5. Use","training_load()","time in zone, distribution"
"5. Use","predict_performance()","race times, with a range"
"5. Use","calibrate_performance()","your own equation"
"6. Compare","compare_tests()","change vs noise"
"6. Compare","curve_shift()","how far the curve moved"
"6. Compare","curve_shape()","shift, or new shape?"
"6. Compare","lactate_trend()","a series of tests"
"6. Compare","relative_thresholds()","per kg, % of peak"
')
collapsibleTree::collapsibleTree(
  steps, hierarchy = c("step", "tool", "detail"), root = "lactater", collapsed = TRUE,
  fill = "#1f5fa8", fontSize = 13, width = "100%", height = 520, zoomable = FALSE
)
```

## Your data

One row per stage of a step test: the intensity (power in W, or speed), the lactate measured at the end of the
stage and, if you have them, the heart rate and the rating of perceived exertion (RPE). A resting sample, if you took
one, is the row with intensity 0.

```{r}
demo_data
```

Rows with a missing lactate (a missed sample) are dropped with a warning. If the last stage was not completed,
enter its time-weighted intensity (as `demo_data` does for its 2-min last stage at 191 W), or leave it out with
`max_intensity`. How to collect data that does the methods justice is in [Best practices for a step
test](https://fmmattioni.github.io/lactater/articles/best-practices.html).

## Estimate the thresholds

```{r}
results <- lactate_threshold(
  demo_data,
  intensity_column = intensity,
  lactate_column = lactate,
  heart_rate_column = heart_rate,
  sport = "cycling",
  plot = FALSE
)
results
```

Every method runs by default. Pick some with `method`, e.g. `method = c("Dmax", "LTP")`. Add `rpe_column` (and
`rpe_scale = "CR10"` for the 0-10 scale) to get the RPE at each threshold.

## Look at them

The overview puts every threshold on the same intensity axis as the curve, one row per method, with a table of the
values at each threshold:

```{r, fig.height = 7.5, fig.width = 8}
autoplot(results)
```

Or look at one method in detail:

```{r}
autoplot(results, method = "ModDmax")
```

## Check the analysis

`lactate_checks()` flags what is easy to miss in a table of numbers, and `lactate_diagnostics()` checks the fitted
curve and how much each threshold rests on single stages:

```{r}
lactate_checks(results)
diagnostics <- lactate_diagnostics(results)
diagnostics
```

```{r, fig.height = 10, fig.width = 9}
autoplot(diagnostics)
```

## How sure are we?

With 7 to 10 samples, a threshold reported to 0.1 W is false precision. `ci = TRUE` adds bootstrap confidence
intervals (this takes a few seconds; use more replicates than this for real work):

```{r}
set.seed(2024)
with_ci <- lactate_threshold(
  demo_data, intensity, lactate, heart_rate,
  method = c("OBLA", "Dmax", "LTP"), plot = FALSE, ci = TRUE, n_boot = 200
)
with_ci[c("method", "intensity", "intensity_low", "intensity_high")]
```

## Training zones

Choose which thresholds mark LT1 and LT2, and three or five zones:

```{r}
zones <- lactate_zones(results, lt1 = "Log-log", lt2 = "Log-Poly-ModDmax", model = 5)
zones
autoplot(zones)
```

## A table for your report

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("gt", quietly = TRUE)}
lactate_report(results)
```

## Many tests at once

Use `.by` with the columns that identify each test. `lactate_tests` holds 15 tests across sports and fitness levels;
here, the six tests of one cyclist:

```{r}
series <- subset(lactate_tests, athlete == "cyclist_series")
lactate_threshold(series, intensity, lactate, method = "Dmax", dmax_methods = "ModDmax", plot = FALSE, .by = "day")
```

## Learn more

* [Best practices for a step test](https://fmmattioni.github.io/lactater/articles/best-practices.html): how to run
  a test and analyze it, as a checklist with sources.
* [The methods and the evidence](https://fmmattioni.github.io/lactater/articles/methods.html): how each method is
  defined and what the evidence says.
* [Checking the analysis](https://fmmattioni.github.io/lactater/articles/checking.html): checks, regression
  diagnostics, and confidence intervals.
* [Training zones](https://fmmattioni.github.io/lactater/articles/zones.html): choosing LT1 and LT2, three and five
  zones.
* [Training load](https://fmmattioni.github.io/lactater/articles/training-load.html): time in zone and intensity
  distribution.
* [Comparing tests](https://fmmattioni.github.io/lactater/articles/compare.html): is a change real, did the curve
  shift or change shape, and trends.
* [Predicting performance](https://fmmattioni.github.io/lactater/articles/performance.html): race times from a step
  test, how sure they are, and your own equation.
* [The example data](https://fmmattioni.github.io/lactater/articles/example-data.html): 15 tests across sports.
* [VLamax](https://fmmattioni.github.io/lactater/articles/beyond-the-step-test.html): the maximal lactate accumulation
  rate from a sprint test.
